svg.title: Request pipeline: the filters an API request passes through, in order
svg.text: How one API request travels through the backend, top to bottom. The response goes back up the same way.
built into Spring Security or Spring MVC
the request stops here and gets this response (as Problem Details)
Bearer token; the register adds X-Device-Id, X-App-Version
HTTPS, HSTS, body size limit, coarse limit per IP
X-Request-Id (or a new one), trace span, log fields
adds HSTS, nosniff, frame-deny to every response
only the admin web origin may call /api/v1
refresh cookie on /api/v1/auth only; bearer APIs skip it
JWT signature (JWKS), expiry, token version ver
Bucket4j: by IP (login, PIN), user (admin), device (sync)
builds CurrentContext: tenant, user, branch, device
device matches token, not locked; app version; tenant
URL rules: public, signed in, device only, support only
POST creating money or stock: same key → stored response
same key again → the stored response
row-level security: only this tenant's rows
no tenant set → no rows (fails closed)
Errors anywhere above become Problem Details with a stable code and the requestId (@RestControllerAdvice).
The response is compressed (gzip/br) and gets security headers and X-Request-Id.
ContextFilter clears the context and the log fields in finally, so nothing leaks to the next request.
RESPONSE GOES BACK UP THROUGH THE SAME FILTERS
